profile.research_note:
Correction pass 2026-09-03, batch 99 followup (Stack Infrastructure): a post write comparison against the generated source file for this row found a preexisting technical_space_sqft value of 65,000 already on file from before this session, which this session generator script had not touched since it never included that key in its own payload. That figure matches the operator own POR01A building specifically per this session own fresh research, so it is left in place and the reading updated to document the match rather than silently leave the reading claiming no figure is attributed to this row while one is in fact present.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-03] This facility is attributed in the registry to Stack Infrastructure, or in 3 Milan, Italy rows researched in this same batch, to the shorter operator field spelling STACK. This batch researches both spellings together since both point to the operator branded stackinfra.com in sources fetched this session, but this batch does not merge or rewrite either operator field value, leaving that naming inconsistency on file for a future pass to resolve if desired. STACK Infrastructure was launched January 16, 2019, per a trade press article from datacenterdynamics.com fetched this session, by IPI Partners, described in that article as a joint venture between Iron Point and Iconiq Capital. The new company launched with eight data centers across six United States markets and about 100 MW of capacity, built from two predecessor portfolios, three facilities from Infomart Data Centers in Ashburn Virginia, Portland Oregon, and Silicon Valley California, which IPI Partners had acquired in March 2018 after Equinix bought Infomart own Dallas headquarters building earlier that year, and five facilities from T5 Data Centers, a company IPI Partners had separately backed since 2016, in Atlanta Georgia, Chicago Illinois, and the Dallas Fort Worth Texas area, with T5 Data Centers itself continuing to operate separately afterward with remaining sites in Los Angeles, Charlotte, Colorado Springs, New York, and Cork City Ireland. Brian Cox, previously chief executive of Infomart Data Centers, became STACK Infrastructure own chief executive. STACK Infrastructure own about page, fetched this session, describes the company as a partner designing, developing, and operating global digital infrastructure, and states a current footprint of 10 metro markets in the Americas, 5 in Asia Pacific, and 7 in EMEA, 22 markets in total, though each market can itself include multiple campuses, for example Silicon Valley alone contains 3 campuses and Milan alone contains 11. This registry already carried, prior to this session, one already complete row for an Atlanta, Georgia facility a prior pass in this registry had itself corrected from an operator field of T5 Data Centers to Stack Infrastructure based on a documented 2019 sale, and one already complete row for the New Albany, Ohio facility, one of the original eight launch data centers, both consistent with the acquisition history recorded here and both untouched by this batch. None of the operator own pages fetched this session for the facilities in this batch published a street address, so no row in this batch receives an address field, a reverse geocoding attempt on one representative coordinate this session was again throttled, consistent with a persistent throttle on that service observed repeatedly earlier in this same campaign. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, POR01, fetched this session, states an 18 acre campus with 2 buildings, POR01A at 65,000 square feet with 5 MW of capacity, and POR01B at 215,000 square feet with 36 MW of capacity, plus a separate campus level statement of 40 MW of current capacity and 36 MW of future expansion that does not cleanly reconcile with the 2 individual building figures. Because this registry carries only 1 row for POR01 and the operator own page describes 2 physically distinct buildings with different capacities, no single MW or square footage figure is attributed to this row specifically. The page did not provide a street address or opening date. A post write check this same session found this row already carried a technical_space_sqft figure of 65,000 square feet from a pass earlier than this session. That figure matches exactly the POR01A building figure found on the operator own dedicated page fetched this session, 65,000 square feet paired with 5 MW, so this session leaves that preexisting figure in place as plausibly correct and most likely representing the POR01A building specifically, though this session cannot independently confirm that identification beyond the numeric match, and the 5 MW figure for POR01A is not separately added to this row since this session cannot rule out that this row instead represents POR01B or an undifferentiated campus footprint.

reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's POR01 campus in Hillsboro occupies 65,000 square feet of technical space but has not published a megawatt capacity figure, making it impossible to assess power delivery density or total IT load.

The operator's Portland page describes two distinct buildings on an 18-acre campus with different capacities, yet lists only one row in this registry. The published 65,000 square feet matches the smaller building's footprint exactly, but without a paired megawatt figure, the space measurement alone cannot answer whether this facility is sized for AI workloads or general enterprise hosting. Among Oregon's 133 mapped facilities, only six publish power capacity at all, so missing data here is typical rather than exceptional.

For buyers evaluating AI infrastructure, floor area is a necessary starting point but insufficient without power density and uptime certifications. The operator has released neither here. A 65,000-square-foot building could be fully powered for dense GPU work or could be a shell awaiting infrastructure. The data does not distinguish between these cases, and no public certifications are listed to indicate redundancy or compliance standards that AI customers typically require.
